$comment: Illustrative machine-readable CBOM profile for a managed service, written by its provider. It extends the Interface Disclosure Baseline, narrowed to the subject type 'service' and the stages 'configured' and 'observed'. A service record cites the product records of the software it runs and joins each interface to the product interface it realises, as a deployment record does. It adds what a customer of a service needs and a deployment record does not carry: the regions covered, key custody on stores of customer data, and where the provider announces changes. The worked example is Keycloak 26.7.3 run as a managed identity service by an illustrative provider.
title: Service Disclosure (Example)

objective.consumer: A customer, or an assessor acting for one, that relies on a service it does not run
objective.decision: Whether to rely on the service, and what to require of the provider in the contract
decisionOptions: rely on the service as offered
rely on it with contractual requirements

scope.$comment: Narrows the base to running services, as configured or observed by the provider.

overrides.note: Raised from MAY: a customer needs to know whether the provider's ingress or the application holds the TLS keys of each customer-facing interface.

productRules.description: Service names the regions the record describes
productRules.note: Part of the coverage statement. Where the cryptography differs between regions, the provider writes one record per group of regions.

productRules.description: Service declares at least one storage interface for customer data, or states why it has none
productRules.note: For most customers the store matters more than the session.

productRules.description: Service cites the records it builds on, each by BOM-Link and hash
productRules.note: The product records of the software it runs, and the records of the services beneath it.

productRules.description: Service states what makes the provider produce a new record
productRules.note: With the document timestamp and the change-notice pointer, a customer's policy can judge whether the record it holds is current.

interfaceRules.note: The key-custody models a tenant can choose for this store.
The custody model a new tenant gets unless it chooses another. The present-state attribute behind keyCustodySupported (C12). A tenant's own choice is stated in its tenant record.
The regions where this store holds customer data.

referenceRules.note: Where the provider announces changes to the service. The context kind is defined in the baseline. A service changes without a version number, so a customer needs this, with the document timestamp and the regeneration trigger (P4), to judge whether the record it holds is current.

exclusions.item: A maximum age for the record
exclusions.reason: Freshness is a policy matter (Release 1). The record supplies what a policy needs.

exclusions.item: The customer's choice of key custody
exclusions.reason: A tenant fact. It belongs in the tenant record, which cites this one.

changelog.summary: Initial version, built on Keycloak run as a managed service.
